title: Statement Maintenance Charge on Retention Statements
content:
Maintenance charge rule — Statement maintenance charge, Payoff and Loan Satisfaction

**When it applies.** On the payoff case of a Borrower Voluntary Payoff requested by the borrower of record on a loan whose maturity case is due and payable, in its extension period or referred to foreclosure; the statement maintenance charge enters the retention statement balance.

**Rule.** The statement maintenance charge is figured from the latest inspection result recorded on the loan's occupancy profile under the Occupancy and Residency Certification product, read with the vacant-property securing setting of the maturity case's plan under the Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases product, and only where that plan permits vacant-property securing: when the result found the home vacant and the loan's property type is FHA-approved condominium or planned unit development, it is the flat USD 120.00 association maintenance charge; when it found the home vacant and the property is of any other type, or is a Summit loan, which records no property type, it is USD 55.00 of monthly maintenance for each of the statement months of vacancy; any other result, no result, or a plan that does not permit vacant-property securing carries nothing (0.00).

**Counting the months.** The statement months of vacancy are the whole calendar months from the occupancy profile's non-occupancy date to the statement date, not below 0, plus one; a profile with no non-occupancy date counts one month.

**Same-day results.** Where several inspection results on the occupancy profile share the latest effective date, a vacant finding among them counts as the latest result, and otherwise an unable-to-determine finding does.

**Basis questions.**

*Does an inspection that could not determine occupancy produce a maintenance charge?* No; only a vacant finding does.

*Does a condominium's charge grow with the months of vacancy?* No; an FHA-approved condominium or planned unit development takes the flat USD 120.00.

*Hypothetical:* a vacant single-family HECM whose non-occupancy date is 10 June and statement date 25 September counts 3 whole months plus one, so USD 220.00.
